metadata.summary: Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren Talks are ongoing over a possible November blockbuster clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua; an apparent dispute over the location of the fight led to Fury claiming that the event was in "serious doubt" Tuesday 25 August 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boxing promoter Frank Warren says he expects to see the much-anticipated heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in early November but says there are still plenty of negotiations that need to happen first. Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt. Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money". A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket. England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain. Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship. Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix. Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort. The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale. messages.text: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested

metadata.summary: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
metadata.content: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences By Adrian Kajumba and Sahil Jaidka Tuesday 25 August 2026 08:59, UK Image: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools. Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors. York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offence

It was their final pre-season friendly and Andoni Iraola's side won the game 2-0 with Jeremy Jacquet impressing on his debut. During the first half there was a disagreement between Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk. The midfielder pressed but Como just passed the ball into the space behind him. Szoboszlai was visibly angry to find Van Dijk had not stepped up to close the gap.
